design:synth.title: One place, constructed twin
design:synth.one_liner: One treated unit; build a comparison from a donor pool.
design:synth.plain_language: One treated unit, many untreated donors. Build a weighted combination of donors that tracks the treated unit before the intervention, and use it afterwards.
design:synth.in_more_depth: This is what you reach for when the treated unit is a country, a region or a firm, and there is no comparable single control. The weights are chosen to reproduce the pre-intervention path, and the restriction that they are non-negative and sum to one is deliberate: it forbids extrapolation. Pre-period fit is the test. A synthetic unit that cannot reproduce the treated unit before the intervention has no claim to reproduce it afterwards, and the estimate is then mostly the pre-existing gap. Inference is by permutation, not by standard errors: re-run the method pretending each donor was treated, and see where the real one ranks.
design:synth.how_the_board_reads: If the synthetic unit cannot reproduce the pre-period, it is not a counterfactual.

what_it_assumes.title: Pre-treatment fit from the donor pool
what_it_assumes.explains: The weighted combination of untreated units reproduces the treated unit's pre-period path closely enough to stand in for it afterwards.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Visible pre-period gaps; a short pre-period relative to the number of donors; one donor carrying most of the weight.

what_it_assumes.title: Treated unit inside the donor convex hull
what_it_assumes.explains: The treated unit's characteristics can be written as a weighted average of the donors', with weights that do not go negative.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treated unit is at an extreme of the donor distribution on the predictors, or the pre-period gap has a persistent level offset.

what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

design:its.title: A shock in a single series
design:its.one_liner: Before versus after an interruption; maybe a control series.
design:its.plain_language: One series, one interruption. Fit the trend before, extrapolate it, and compare with what happened.
design:its.in_more_depth: Common in public health, where a rule changes nationally and there is no untreated region. The strength is that the unit is its own control; the weakness is that the counterfactual is entirely a modelling assumption, and an extrapolated linear trend over several years is a strong claim. Three things routinely go wrong. Seasonality left unmodelled shows up as an effect. Autocorrelated residuals make the confidence interval far too narrow. And anything else that changed on the same date is inseparable from the policy -- which is why a control series that should not have been affected is worth a great deal.
design:its.how_the_board_reads: The counterfactual trend is an assumption, not an estimate.

what_it_assumes.title: No co-interventions at the interruption
what_it_assumes.explains: Nothing else changed at the same moment that also moves the outcome.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: A busy policy period; a national event at the same date; a change in how the outcome was measured or coded at the same date.

what_it_assumes.title: Functional form of the counterfactual trend
what_it_assumes.explains: The line you fit before the interruption is the line the outcome would have continued to follow.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Few pre-period points; residual autocorrelation that survives the model; the estimate flips when you add a seasonal term or a quadratic trend.

design:mediation.title: How it worked (pathways)
design:mediation.one_liner: We care about a mediator, not only the total effect.
design:mediation.plain_language: Not just whether the treatment worked, but how much of the effect travelled through a particular mechanism.
design:mediation.in_more_depth: Mediation needs two exchangeability assumptions rather than one, and the second is harder than the first: even in a randomised trial, the mediator is not randomised, so whatever determines it may also drive the outcome. Natural direct and indirect effects need a third condition comparing outcomes across worlds no person can inhabit at once. It is not testable, even in principle. Interventional effects replace it with something a trial could implement, which is why they are the better default for policy and health questions. Do not start from a product of two regression coefficients. It is only the indirect effect under linearity and no interaction, and it is silent about the assumptions.
design:mediation.how_the_board_reads: You have to believe you measured everything that confounds treatment with the outcome AND everything that confounds the mediator with the outcome. That second half is the hard one, and it is what statisticians call sequential ignorability.

what_it_assumes.title: Sequential ignorability
what_it_assumes.explains: No unmeasured confounding of the treatment-outcome relationship, and none of the mediator-outcome relationship either, even after conditioning on treatment.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There is a variable affected by treatment that also confounds the mediator-outcome relationship. Under that structure the natural effects are not identified at all.

what_it_assumes.title: Exchangeability / no unmeasured confounding
what_it_assumes.explains: Treated and untreated units are comparable once you condition on the confounders you measured. Everything that pushed people towards treatment and also moves the outcome is in your adjustment set.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Treatment was chosen by people who knew something about the likely outcome that you do not observe. Clinical judgement, self-selection into a programme, and administrative triage are the classic cases.

what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

design:longitudinal.title: Treatment that changes over time
design:longitudinal.one_liner: The same person is treated, untreated, treated again; confounders also move.
design:longitudinal.plain_language: The same unit is treated, untreated, treated again -- and the confounders move too, partly because of the treatment.
design:longitudinal.in_more_depth: This is the setting ordinary regression cannot handle. A variable like blood pressure or employment status is a consequence of past treatment and a cause of future treatment. Adjust for it and you block part of the effect and open a collider path; ignore it and confounding remains. G-methods solve it by modelling the treatment process over time instead of conditioning on its consequences: inverse-probability weighting for a marginal structural model, the parametric g-formula, or a sequential doubly robust estimator. Lag discipline is the practical rule, and the board enforces it: a covariate may adjust a treatment decision only if it was measured before that decision. Arrows cannot point into the past.
design:longitudinal.how_the_board_reads: Treatment and confounders both move over time, and each can only be affected by what came before it. Whether a covariate is treated as measured at the same time as the treatment or one period earlier changes the answer, so say which you mean.

what_it_assumes.title: No unmeasured time-varying confounding
what_it_assumes.explains: At every period, the things that drive the treatment decision and also affect the outcome are measured -- and measured before that decision.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Clinical measurements taken after the dose was changed; employment status recorded at the end of a period used to explain treatment at its start.

designs.title: Adjust for background differences
designs.one_liner: Treatment was not random; we can measure the things that made people get it.

designs.title: Randomised or as-if randomised
designs.one_liner: People were assigned by chance, or as good as chance.

designs.title: Something else pushed people in
designs.one_liner: An instrument or encouragement changed treatment, not the outcome directly.

estimands.title: Average treatment effect
estimands.one_liner: If everyone got the programme, how would the average outcome change?

estimands.title: Average treatment effect on the treated
estimands.one_liner: For people who actually got it, what did it do?

what_it_assumes.title: Exchangeability / no unmeasured confounding
what_it_assumes.explains: Treated and untreated units are comparable once you condition on the confounders you measured. Everything that pushed people towards treatment and also moves the outcome is in your adjustment set.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Treatment was chosen by people who knew something about the likely outcome that you do not observe. Clinical judgement, self-selection into a programme, and administrative triage are the classic cases.

what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

what_it_assumes.title: Randomisation held
what_it_assumes.explains: Assignment really was by chance, and nothing after assignment broke the comparison -- no differential dropout, no crossover you have not modelled.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Dropout differs across arms; take-up is far from assignment; the randomiser was a person with discretion.

what_it_assumes.title: Instrument relevance
what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument actually moves treatment, and moves it enough that the resulting estimate is not mostly noise.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: An effective F below about 10; a first-stage coefficient that is substantively tiny even if statistically significant; many instruments.

what_it_assumes.title: Exclusion restriction
what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment. On the board, that is the arrow you did not draw.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is a policy that changed several things at once; it is correlated with geography, time or institutions that have their own effects; it was chosen because it predicted the outcome.

what_it_assumes.title: Monotonicity / no defiers
what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument pushes everyone the same way, or not at all. Nobody takes the treatment only because they were discouraged from it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is an incentive that could plausibly backfire for some people, or it is a judge or examiner whose leniency ordering differs across case types.

when_to_use: The honest floor. When the point estimate rests on assumptions nobody can defend, an interval that rests on almost none is worth more than a number that rests on many.
when_not_to_use: The bounds are often wide enough to include zero, which is informative and unpopular. Narrowing them means adding assumptions, and those should be stated.

availability.summary: Not built yet. The card is here so you can see that the method exists and read what it is for.
availability.coming: Not implemented. Designed for: the spec and result schema already allow an interval with no point estimate.

references: Manski (1990), Nonparametric bounds on treatment effects

what_it_assumes.title: Parallel trends
what_it_assumes.explains: Without the policy, treated and comparison groups would have moved the same way. Not that they were at the same level -- that their paths would have been parallel.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Pre-period event-study coefficients drift away from zero; the policy was adopted because outcomes were already moving; the groups differ in composition in ways that interact with time.

what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: It uses every untreated cell in the panel to build the counterfactual, which makes it the most efficient of the staggered estimators when the unit-and-period model is right. The logic is also the easiest to say out loud: what happened, minus what the untreated cells say would have.
when_not_to_use: It leans harder on the additive unit-plus-period model than the 2x2 estimators do -- if untreated paths are not parallel, that shows up as effect rather than as a failed diagnostic. Pre-period effects are zero by construction unless periods are held out, so a test on a model that saw the pre-period is not a test.

options.name: pre_test_periods
options.label: Pre-adoption periods to hold out for testing
options.help: The comparison model is fitted on the pre-period, so pre-period 'effects' are near zero by construction unless some periods are held out. These held-out periods are what the parallel-trends test is actually run on. Units that would lose their last untreated period keep it.

options.name: max_lag
options.label: Periods after adoption to show separately
options.help: Anything later is pooled into the last point, so no observation is dropped.

options.name: covariate_mode
options.label: How covariates enter the comparison model
options.help: Additive shifts the untreated path by a constant. By period lets each covariate matter differently in each period, which is the Wooldridge-Mundlak form and much more flexible -- and much hungrier for data.

options.name: ci_level
options.label: Confidence level
options.help: Width of the interval reported next to the estimate.

when_to_use: Under staggered adoption this is the default. Nothing that is already treated is ever used as a comparison, the cohort effects are shown next to the average, and the aggregation is a choice you make rather than one a regression makes for you.
when_not_to_use: The comparison group can be thin: with few never-treated units every cohort leans on the same handful of places, and the interval will not tell you that. Cells with one or two treated units become case studies wearing a standard error. A pre-adoption test that does not reject is usually low power, not evidence.

options.name: control_group
options.label: Compare adopters with
options.help: Units that never adopt are the cleanest comparison. Units that have not adopted yet give you more of them, at the cost of assuming the late adopters were on the same path. If nobody stays untreated the estimator switches to not-yet-treated on its own and says so.

options.name: est_method
options.label: How each 2x2 adjusts for covariates
options.help: Doubly robust uses an outcome model and a comparison-group model together and is right if either is. IPW reweights the comparison group; Reg models the change in the outcome. With no covariates all three are the same plain difference of differences.

options.name: aggregation
options.label: Headline average
options.help: Simple weights every treated cohort-period by cohort size. Group averages each cohort's own effect. Dynamic averages the periods since adoption. Calendar averages the years. They answer different questions and all four are reported.

options.name: base_period
options.label: Measure each period against
options.help: Universal compares every period with the one just before adoption, which is what the event-study picture usually means. Varying compares each pre-period with the period before it, which shows period-to-period drift instead of accumulated drift.

options.name: cband
options.label: Simultaneous band on the event study
options.help: A pointwise interval is right for one period and wrong for the picture: read five periods at once and one will fall outside by chance. This widens the band so the whole path is covered together.

options.name: boot_reps
options.label: Bootstrap draws
options.help: Multiplier-bootstrap draws for the simultaneous band. Seeded by the run seed, so the band is reproducible.

options.name: clip
options.label: Clip comparison-group probabilities at
options.help: Bounds the weights when a unit is almost certain to be in the adopting cohort. Clipping is counted and reported, never silent.

options.name: ci_level
options.label: Confidence level
options.help: Width of the interval reported next to the estimate.

when_to_use: When parallel trends is only credible after conditioning on covariates, this is the estimator that does the conditioning properly: it is consistent if the model for the comparison group's change is right, or if the model for who adopted is right.
when_not_to_use: Doubly robust is not doubly safe. When some units are almost certain to be adopters, the weights blow up and the outcome model quietly takes over by extrapolation. Adoption is staggered -- the doubly robust 2x2 still works cohort by cohort, but did.callaway_santanna is the same thing with the aggregations and the simultaneous bands.

what_it_assumes.title: Parallel trends
what_it_assumes.explains: Without the policy, treated and comparison groups would have moved the same way. Not that they were at the same level -- that their paths would have been parallel.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Pre-period event-study coefficients drift away from zero; the policy was adopted because outcomes were already moving; the groups differ in composition in ways that interact with time.

what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: It is the picture policy readers actually read: pre-period points that hover around zero, and a visible break at adoption. It shows dynamics instead of averaging them away.
when_not_to_use: A pre-trend test that fails to reject is not proof of parallel trends -- it is often just a wide interval. Under staggered adoption each lead and lag is contaminated by already-treated units used as controls (Sun and Abraham 2021). The headline number here is a simple unweighted average of the post-period coefficients, not a cohort-size weighted ATT.

options.name: ref_period

options.help: Every coefficient is measured against this period, relative to adoption. -1 is the period just before treatment; choose -2 if you suspect the policy was anticipated.

options.name: max_lag

options.name: absorb
options.label: How to handle the fixed effects
options.help: Auto uses dummy variables on small panels and partials the fixed effects out on large ones. The estimate is the same either way; this only trades memory for speed.

options.name: ci_level
options.label: Confidence level
options.help: Width of the interval reported next to the estimate.

options.name: wild_bootstrap
options.label: Wild cluster bootstrap when clusters are few
options.help: Below 30 clusters the ordinary cluster-robust p-value rejects too often. This adds a restricted wild cluster bootstrap p-value in the Sensitivity tab.

options.name: wild_reps
options.label: Bootstrap draws
options.help: Rademacher draws for the wild cluster bootstrap. Seeded by the run seed.

when_to_use: It looks and reads like the regression people expect, but the fixed effects are learned where the policy is off, so treated cells cannot bend them. Covariates can enter period by period, which is the Wooldridge-Mundlak form that handles covariate-specific trends.
when_not_to_use: The second stage is a regression on residuals from a first stage, so its ordinary standard error is too small; the correction is applied here, but any tool that skips it will look more precise than it is. With no covariates it is numerically the imputation estimator, so reporting both as independent confirmation would be double counting.

when_to_use: It is the fastest way to see whether a staggered two-way fixed effects number is trustworthy. If most of the weight sits on later-versus-earlier-treated comparisons, the estimate is telling you about the weighting scheme rather than the policy.
when_not_to_use: This is arithmetic, not an estimator: the weights have no standard errors, and the headline number it decomposes is still the two-way fixed effects estimate with all of its problems. Simplifications named in the printout: balanced panel only, binary absorbing treatment, always-treated units dropped rather than used as an extra comparison group, and covariates ignored.
Every unit adopts on the same date -- then there is a single comparison and nothing to decompose.

when_to_use: It is the event-study picture people already read, repaired. The saturated cohort-by-period terms make it impossible for one cohort to serve as another's control, which is the contamination that makes an ordinary event study misleading under staggered adoption.
when_not_to_use: Saturating cohort by relative period costs a lot of parameters, so with many cohorts and short panels the individual points get noisy. Without a never-treated group the last cohort becomes the comparison and its own effect is absorbed into the period effects, biasing everything else.

what_it_assumes.title: Pre-treatment fit from the donor pool
what_it_assumes.explains: The weighted combination of untreated units reproduces the treated unit's pre-period path closely enough to stand in for it afterwards.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Visible pre-period gaps; a short pre-period relative to the number of donors; one donor carrying most of the weight.

what_it_assumes.title: Treated unit inside the donor convex hull
what_it_assumes.explains: The treated unit's characteristics can be written as a weighted average of the donors', with weights that do not go negative.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treated unit is at an extreme of the donor distribution on the predictors, or the pre-period gap has a persistent level offset.

when_to_use: Relaxes the parallel-trends requirement to hold only for a weighted subset, and the reference implementation carries the authors' own inference.
when_not_to_use: Inference relies on a jackknife or placebo scheme that needs a reasonable number of treated units.

what_it_assumes.title: Parallel trends
what_it_assumes.explains: Without the policy, treated and comparison groups would have moved the same way. Not that they were at the same level -- that their paths would have been parallel.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Pre-period event-study coefficients drift away from zero; the policy was adopted because outcomes were already moving; the groups differ in composition in ways that interact with time.

what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: When something else was happening in the treated units at the same time, the third difference sweeps it out: any shock that hit both groups inside a unit and period equally cancels. It rescues designs where plain parallel trends is not credible.
when_not_to_use: It buys robustness with a new assumption: the gap between the two groups inside a unit must have been on parallel paths. If the policy also affected the supposedly unaffected group -- spillovers, general equilibrium -- the third difference subtracts part of the effect. Under staggered adoption the same weighting critique as two-way fixed effects applies, and there is no Callaway-Sant'Anna style version here.
The third dimension does not vary inside a unit and period -- then it is effect heterogeneity across units, not a third difference.

when_to_use: When one group is treated at one date, this is the whole design and everyone can see the four numbers it is made of. Nothing is hidden inside a fixed-effects machine.

method:discovery.structure_learning.title: Structure learning (causal discovery)
method:discovery.structure_learning.one_liner: Search for a graph consistent with the data. It does not recover the true causal structure from observational data without extra assumptions.

designs.title: Adjust for background differences
designs.one_liner: Treatment was not random; we can measure the things that made people get it.

what_it_assumes.title: Exchangeability / no unmeasured confounding
what_it_assumes.explains: Treated and untreated units are comparable once you condition on the confounders you measured. Everything that pushed people towards treatment and also moves the outcome is in your adjustment set.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Treatment was chosen by people who knew something about the likely outcome that you do not observe. Clinical judgement, self-selection into a programme, and administrative triage are the classic cases.

what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: null
when_not_to_use: Discovery algorithms return an equivalence class of graphs, not a graph, and the class is usually large. Different algorithms on the same data return different answers, and none of them can see a confounder you did not measure.
Always, as a substitute for a design. It is a hypothesis generator behind a gate, and anything it produces lands as a candidate graph you must accept.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

when_to_use: When the series has real memory - last month's value predicts this month's beyond any trend - segmented regression leaves that correlation in the residuals and only patches the standard errors. An ARIMA models it, and its pre-period forecast is an honest, widening counterfactual band.
when_not_to_use: The order is chosen by AIC, and near-ties are common; different orders can move the intervention coefficient. Nothing here tests causality: the coefficient is just the size of shift the model wants at that date. Standard errors are asymptotic and optimistic in short series. Simplifications, stated plainly: the search is a small two-stage AIC grid rather than full stepwise auto.arima, no seasonal unit-root test is run, and this is not CausalImpact - there is no Bayesian structural time series and no posterior.
Fewer than about 30 pre-interruption periods, where ARIMA orders are not identified

when_to_use: Handles trend, seasonality and control series in one model, and the posterior over the cumulative effect is easier to read than a sequence of coefficients.

when_to_use: A single interrupted series cannot tell your intervention apart from anything else that happened that month. A control series that was not exposed can, and the control's own level and slope change are reported so you can see whether the shock was shared.
when_not_to_use: It trades one assumption for another: instead of assuming the trend would have continued, you assume the two series would have moved in parallel. Simplification: the interacted model uses Driscoll-Kraay standard errors, which lean on having a reasonable number of periods and are thin on the cross-sectional side when there are only two or three series.

what_it_assumes.explains: The line you fit before the interruption is the line the outcome would have continued to follow.

what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.

what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.

when_to_use: It is the standard public-health ITS, it is transparent enough that a reader can check it by eye against the plotted series, and it separates an immediate jump from a change of direction instead of blurring the two into one number.
when_not_to_use: The counterfactual is a straight line projected forward, and nothing in the data tests it. Anything else that happened at the same date is inside the estimate. Autocorrelated residuals make plain intervals far too narrow, so HAC is the default and the Ljung-Box test is not optional. A regular seasonal cycle that peaks near the interruption will be read as an effect unless you model it. With fewer than about eight pre-period points there is no trend to project. Simplification: the HAC lag is the conventional rule, not a data-driven optimal bandwidth.

designs.one_liner: An instrument or encouragement changed treatment, not the outcome directly.

estimands.one_liner: For people who only got it because of the instrument or the cutoff, what did it do?

estimands.title: Complier average causal effect
estimands.one_liner: For the people who comply with what they were offered, what did it do?

estimands.title: Average treatment effect
estimands.one_liner: If everyone got the programme, how would the average outcome change?

what_it_assumes.title: Instrument relevance
what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument actually moves treatment, and moves it enough that the resulting estimate is not mostly noise.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: An effective F below about 10; a first-stage coefficient that is substantively tiny even if statistically significant; many instruments.

what_it_assumes.title: Exclusion restriction
what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment. On the board, that is the arrow you did not draw.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is a policy that changed several things at once; it is correlated with geography, time or institutions that have their own effects; it was chosen because it predicted the outcome.

what_it_assumes.title: Monotonicity / no defiers
what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument pushes everyone the same way, or not at all. Nobody takes the treatment only because they were discouraged from it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is an incentive that could plausibly backfire for some people, or it is a judge or examiner whose leniency ordering differs across case types.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: The standard instrumental-variables estimator, and the one every referee reads without translation. With a strong first stage it is efficient and its interval is honest.
when_not_to_use: Exclusion is untestable and usually the weakest link: if the instrument reaches the outcome by any other route, the bias is the violation divided by the first stage, which is enormous when the instrument is weak. Two-stage least squares is also the estimator that degrades worst under weak instruments: it is biased towards ordinary least squares and its interval is too short.
The Olea-Pflueger effective first-stage F is below about 10; report the Anderson-Rubin set instead.

what_it_assumes.title: Instrument relevance
what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument actually moves treatment, and moves it enough that the resulting estimate is not mostly noise.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: An effective F below about 10; a first-stage coefficient that is substantively tiny even if statistically significant; many instruments.

what_it_assumes.title: Exclusion restriction
what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment. On the board, that is the arrow you did not draw.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is a policy that changed several things at once; it is correlated with geography, time or institutions that have their own effects; it was chosen because it predicted the outcome.

what_it_assumes.title: Monotonicity / no defiers
what_it_assumes.explains: The instrument pushes everyone the same way, or not at all. Nobody takes the treatment only because they were discouraged from it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The instrument is an incentive that could plausibly backfire for some people, or it is a judge or examiner whose leniency ordering differs across case types.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: With more instruments than endogenous variables and genuinely heteroskedastic errors, the efficient weight matrix buys real precision, and the Hansen J statistic comes with it.
when_not_to_use: Exclusion is untestable and usually the weakest link: if the instrument reaches the outcome by any other route, the bias is the violation divided by the first stage, which is enormous when the instrument is weak. The efficient weight matrix has to be estimated, and in small samples that estimate is noisy enough to bias the coefficients and shrink the standard errors below the truth.
Small samples with many instruments: the estimated weight matrix does more harm than the efficiency gain is worth.

what_it_assumes.title: No unmeasured time-varying confounding
what_it_assumes.explains: At every period, the things that drive the treatment decision and also affect the outcome are measured -- and measured before that decision.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Clinical measurements taken after the dose was changed; employment status recorded at the end of a period used to explain treatment at its start.

what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.title: Sequential ignorability
what_it_assumes.explains: No unmeasured confounding of the treatment-outcome relationship, and none of the mediator-outcome relationship either, even after conditioning on treatment.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There is a variable affected by treatment that also confounds the mediator-outcome relationship. Under that structure the natural effects are not identified at all.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: More robust to positivity violations than weighting, because it does not divide by a treatment probability.
when_not_to_use: Requires a correctly specified blip function, and the estimating equations can have multiple roots.

probes.title: Subset stability
probes.one_liner: Re-estimate on random subsets. The answer should move about as much as losing that much data costs, and no more.

designs.one_liner: The same person is treated, untreated, treated again; confounders also move.

estimands.title: Average treatment effect
estimands.one_liner: If everyone got the programme, how would the average outcome change?

what_it_assumes.title: No unmeasured time-varying confounding
what_it_assumes.explains: At every period, the things that drive the treatment decision and also affect the outcome are measured -- and measured before that decision.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Clinical measurements taken after the dose was changed; employment status recorded at the end of a period used to explain treatment at its start.

what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.title: Sequential ignorability
what_it_assumes.explains: No unmeasured confounding of the treatment-outcome relationship, and none of the mediator-outcome relationship either, even after conditioning on treatment.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There is a variable affected by treatment that also confounds the mediator-outcome relationship. Under that structure the natural effects are not identified at all.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: The standard answer to time-varying confounding, and the one whose failure mode is visible: the weight histogram and the effective sample size tell you when the data cannot support the comparison.
when_not_to_use: Weights are a product over the whole history, so they degenerate as follow-up lengthens; a handful of people end up carrying the estimate while the interval stays narrow.
Long follow-up with strong time-varying confounding, where the cumulative weights collapse the effective sample

when_to_use: The standard way to ask who benefits without fishing: honest sample splitting inside every tree, out-of-bag predictions, and a calibration test that tells you whether the ranking is real.
when_not_to_use: A forest will always return a spread of effects, including when there is none. Read the calibration slope and the RATE before describing heterogeneity. This implementation has no pointwise intervals on the per-unit effects, and its splitting labels are a one-step approximation of grf's. Machine learning does not identify anything. Cross-fitting removes the bias that comes from fitting flexible models on the same rows you estimate with; it does nothing about a confounder you never measured.
Small samples: honesty spends half of every tree's rows on estimation, so under a few hundred rows the leaves are mostly the overall effect.

options.name: learner
options.label: Nuisance learner
options.help: The model used for E[Y|X] and E[D|X]. Boring is usually right: a regularised linear model is hard to beat when the sample is small, and a flexible learner cannot fix a confounder you did not measure.

options.name: folds
options.label: Cross-fitting folds
options.help: Each fold is scored by models that never saw it. More folds use the data better and cost more time; below 5 the estimate starts to depend on the split.

options.name: clip
options.label: Clip propensity scores at
options.help: Keeps the weights finite when a unit is nearly certain to be treated. Every clipped unit is reported, because clipping quietly changes the population.

options.name: ci_level
options.label: Confidence level
options.help: The interval width. Changing it after seeing the result is not a neutral act.

options.name: stability_reps
options.label: Repeat under new fold splits
options.help: Reruns the whole cross-fitting under fresh random splits. The split is an arbitrary choice; the answer should not depend on it.

options.name: rate_reps
options.label: Bootstrap draws for the RATE curve
options.help: Draws used for the standard error of the targeting curve. 0 skips it.

options.name: subgroups
options.label: Pre-registered subgroups
options.help: Groups you named BEFORE looking. Each one gets the same doubly robust score as the headline, and the multiplicity caution comes with them.

options.name: estimand
options.label: Population for the headline average
options.help: The per-unit effects are the point of the method; this is the population the single headline number averages over.

options.name: n_trees
options.label: Trees
options.help: More trees means a smoother, more stable set of per-unit effects. It does not buy you significance.

options.name: min_leaf
options.label: Minimum rows per leaf
options.help: Larger leaves mean steadier but blunter effects. Because of honesty, a leaf needs enough rows on BOTH sides of the split to be usable.

options.name: max_depth
options.label: Maximum tree depth (0 = unlimited)
options.help: A cap on how finely the forest may cut the population.

options.name: subsample_fraction
options.label: Rows per tree
options.help: The share of the sample each tree draws, without replacement. The rest are that tree's out-of-bag rows.

options.name: honest_fraction
options.label: Share of a tree's rows that choose the splits
options.help: The remainder estimate the leaves. Splitting these two jobs is what stops the forest from reading its own noise as heterogeneity.

options.name: mtry
options.label: Variables tried per split
options.help: Trying fewer variables at each split makes the trees more different from one another, which can help when there are many modifiers.

what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: No restriction on how the effect varies, two chances to get the adjustment right, and a standard error from the score's own influence function. This is the default causal ML estimator for a binary treatment.
when_not_to_use: Doubly robust is not doubly safe. When propensities approach 0 or 1 the weights explode, clipping kicks in, and the estimand quietly becomes something about a population you did not choose. The run reports how many units were clipped and at what threshold. Machine learning does not identify anything. Cross-fitting removes the bias that comes from fitting flexible models on the same rows you estimate with; it does nothing about a confounder you never measured.
Fewer than about 200 rows, where cross-fitting has too little to work with.

what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: The one causal ML method that also handles a continuous dose, with an analytic standard error that comes from the estimator's own orthogonal score rather than a bootstrap.
when_not_to_use: It assumes one effect for everyone. With a binary treatment and a varying effect it returns a variance-weighted average that is not the ATE. If the confounders predict treatment almost perfectly there is no residual variation left to divide by, and the interval collapses into nonsense. Machine learning does not identify anything. Cross-fitting removes the bias that comes from fitting flexible models on the same rows you estimate with; it does nothing about a confounder you never measured.
The effect plainly varies across units -- use ml.dml_irm instead.

when_to_use: Comparing meta-learners on the same folds is the cheapest way to see how much of your 'heterogeneity' is the learner rather than the world.

what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

what_it_assumes.title: Parallel trends
what_it_assumes.explains: Without the policy, treated and comparison groups would have moved the same way. Not that they were at the same level -- that their paths would have been parallel.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Pre-period event-study coefficients drift away from zero; the policy was adopted because outcomes were already moving; the groups differ in composition in ways that interact with time.

what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.title: No unmeasured time-varying confounding
what_it_assumes.explains: At every period, the things that drive the treatment decision and also affect the outcome are measured -- and measured before that decision.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Clinical measurements taken after the dose was changed; employment status recorded at the end of a period used to explain treatment at its start.

what_it_assumes.title: Sequential ignorability
what_it_assumes.explains: No unmeasured confounding of the treatment-outcome relationship, and none of the mediator-outcome relationship either, even after conditioning on treatment.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There is a variable affected by treatment that also confounds the mediator-outcome relationship. Under that structure the natural effects are not identified at all.

when_to_use: Complete-case analysis is unbiased only under strong conditions, and this product logs how many rows it costs you on every run. Imputation uses them instead.
when_not_to_use: The imputation model has to be compatible with the analysis model, including its interactions; imputing the outcome and then matching on it is a common and serious error.

what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: Simple, transparent, and the natural baseline when the covariates are few and the groups genuinely overlap.
when_not_to_use: It extrapolates silently. Where treated and untreated units do not overlap, the model invents the comparison and nothing in the output tells you.

what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: Doubly robust like AIPW, but the estimate is a prediction from a model, so it stays inside the bounds of the outcome -- a weighted estimator can return a risk difference no data could produce.
when_not_to_use: The targeting step is driven by inverse propensity weights, so extreme propensities move the estimate a long way and the interval with it. The run reports how far the targeting moved the number and whether the score equation was actually solved. Machine learning does not identify anything. Cross-fitting removes the bias that comes from fitting flexible models on the same rows you estimate with; it does nothing about a confounder you never measured.
Overlap is so poor that most units sit at the propensity clip; then the fluctuation is fitting the boundary, not the data.

options.name: learner
options.label: Nuisance learner
options.help: The model used for E[Y|X] and E[D|X]. Boring is usually right: a regularised linear model is hard to beat when the sample is small, and a flexible learner cannot fix a confounder you did not measure.

options.name: folds
options.label: Cross-fitting folds
options.help: Each fold is scored by models that never saw it. More folds use the data better and cost more time; below 5 the estimate starts to depend on the split.

options.name: clip
options.label: Clip propensity scores at
options.help: Keeps the weights finite when a unit is nearly certain to be treated. Every clipped unit is reported, because clipping quietly changes the population.

options.name: ci_level
options.label: Confidence level
options.help: The interval width. Changing it after seeing the result is not a neutral act.

options.name: stability_reps
options.label: Repeat under new fold splits
options.help: Reruns the whole cross-fitting under fresh random splits. The split is an arbitrary choice; the answer should not depend on it.

options.name: rate_reps
options.label: Bootstrap draws for the RATE curve
options.help: Draws used for the standard error of the targeting curve. 0 skips it.

options.name: subgroups
options.label: Pre-registered subgroups
options.help: Groups you named BEFORE looking. Each one gets the same doubly robust score as the headline, and the multiplicity caution comes with them.

options.name: estimand
options.label: Population
options.help: ATE is everyone; ATT is the units that actually got treated.

options.name: bound_padding
options.label: Padding on the outcome bounds
options.help: Continuous outcomes are squeezed into [0, 1] using the observed range before the targeting step. Padding widens that range if you expect values outside the sample's own minimum and maximum.

what_it_assumes.title: Exchangeability / no unmeasured confounding
what_it_assumes.explains: Treated and untreated units are comparable once you condition on the confounders you measured. Everything that pushed people towards treatment and also moves the outcome is in your adjustment set.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Treatment was chosen by people who knew something about the likely outcome that you do not observe. Clinical judgement, self-selection into a programme, and administrative triage are the classic cases.

what_it_assumes.title: Positivity / overlap
what_it_assumes.explains: Every kind of unit had some chance of being treated and some chance of not being treated. Where that fails, there is no comparison to make and the model is inventing one.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Any single weight carries a large share of the total; the effective sample is far below the nominal one; the propensity model separates the arms almost perfectly; treated units sit outside the control group's range.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: Handles non-linearity and interactions in the treatment model without you specifying them.
when_not_to_use: A flexible propensity model fitted in-sample sharpens the overlap picture artificially; the stopping rule is doing a lot of work.

when_to_use: Take-up was imperfect, so the difference between the arms measures the offer and not the programme. Reporting only one of the two numbers hides which question was answered.
when_not_to_use: The CACE needs the exclusion restriction -- the offer must not affect the outcome except through take-up, which unblinded trials break routinely -- and monotonicity, which cannot be tested. The delta-method interval degrades as the first stage weakens; the bootstrap interval is reported alongside for that reason. No weak-instrument-robust (Anderson-Rubin) set is computed here.
Take-up moves by less than a few percentage points -- the ratio is then a small denominator away from meaningless; report the ITT.

when_to_use: Assignment happened to whole groups, so outcomes inside a group are not independent draws. Treating rows as independent would make the interval far too narrow.
when_not_to_use: Cluster-robust standard errors are justified by the number of clusters, not the number of rows: with fewer than about forty they are too small even with CR2. when_to_use: The randomisation is the only thing this p-value relies on. No normal approximation, no large-sample argument, no variance model -- which matters most exactly when the sample is small, the outcome is skewed, or there are few clusters.
when_not_to_use: It tests the sharp null that treatment changed nothing for anyone, which is not the null that the average effect is zero; rejecting it is a weaker statement than it looks. The permutation scheme must match how assignment was actually done -- miss the blocks or the clusters and the p-value is wrong in a way no amount of computation fixes. Small designs admit few distinct assignments, which puts a floor under the p-value. The interval, when produced, assumes a constant additive effect.

when_not_to_use: Block fixed effects silently report a precision-weighted average rather than the ATE when the treated share differs across blocks. Blocks with one unit in an arm give no within-block variance, so the standard error leans on a pooled approximation this adapter names in its printout. Blocks with only one arm are dropped, which narrows the population the estimate describes.
The blocks were not part of the randomisation -- blocking after the fact on a variable measured post-treatment is not stratification.

what_it_assumes.title: No manipulation of the running variable

what_it_assumes.title: Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff
what_it_assumes.explains: Everything else that affects the outcome changes smoothly through the cutoff, so the only thing that jumps is the treatment.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: It is the RD version of a balance table, and it uses exactly the estimator that produced the headline number, at exactly the same bandwidth. A covariate that jumps is the clearest possible evidence that something other than eligibility changes at the threshold.

options.help: 'mse' is capy's own finite-sample plug-in rule: it measures the bias and variance of this estimator on this sample. 'ik' is the Imbens-Kalyanaraman (2012) formula, for a sharp local linear fit only. Neither is rdrobust's CCT selector.

options.name: bandwidth
options.label: Bandwidth (leave empty to choose one)
options.help: The half-width of the window either side of the cutoff, in the units of the running variable. Setting it by hand overrides the selector; the sensitivity path shows you what every other choice would have given.

options.name: donut
options.label: Donut hole radius
options.help: Drop units within this distance of the cutoff, where heaping and manipulation live. Every dropped row appears in the sample flow.

options.name: kernel
options.label: Weighting near the cutoff
options.help: Triangular gives the most weight to units closest to the cutoff, which is what the MSE-optimal theory assumes. Uniform is the plain 'everyone inside the window counts equally' choice.

options.name: pilot_bandwidth
options.label: Bias-correction pilot bandwidth
options.help: The wider window used by the higher-order fit that estimates the smoothing bias.

options.name: covariate_adjust
options.label: Put the covariates in the local regression
options.help: Off by default: in RD the covariates are how you check the design, not how you fix it. Turning this on tightens the interval a little and slightly changes the estimand.

options.name: vce
options.label: Standard errors
options.help: Heteroskedasticity-robust. HC3 is more conservative in small windows. Set the cluster role as well and the variance becomes cluster-robust.

options.name: ci_level
options.label: Confidence level
options.help: 0.95 unless you have a reason.

options.name: plot_bins
options.label: Bins per side in the plot
options.help: 0 picks about 2 n^(1/3) bins a side.

options.name: plot_bin_spacing
options.label: Bin spacing
options.help: Quantile bins hold the same number of units each; even bins hold the same width each.

what_it_assumes.title: No manipulation of the running variable
what_it_assumes.explains: People could not precisely control which side of the cutoff they landed on.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: A visible spike or gap in the density at the cutoff; covariates that jump; a cutoff that people knew about and had time to respond to.

what_it_assumes.title: Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff
what_it_assumes.explains: Everything else that affects the outcome changes smoothly through the cutoff, so the only thing that jumps is the treatment.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Several rules share the threshold; the running variable is coarse, so "at the cutoff" is really a wide band; the estimate depends heavily on the bandwidth.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: The natural approach when the running variable is discrete with few mass points, where local polynomial inference is fragile.
when_not_to_use: The window has to be chosen by a covariate-balance criterion, and the resulting sample is often tiny, so randomisation inference rather than a normal approximation is required.

what_it_assumes.title: Pre-treatment fit from the donor pool
what_it_assumes.explains: The weighted combination of untreated units reproduces the treated unit's pre-period path closely enough to stand in for it afterwards.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Visible pre-period gaps; a short pre-period relative to the number of donors; one donor carrying most of the weight.

what_it_assumes.title: Treated unit inside the donor convex hull
what_it_assumes.explains: The treated unit's characteristics can be written as a weighted average of the donors', with weights that do not go negative.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treated unit is at an extreme of the donor distribution on the predictors, or the pre-period gap has a persistent level offset.

what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

when_to_use: For one treated unit and a run of pre-treatment periods this is the standard, and its output is legible to non-specialists: a line, a shadow line, and the distance between them. The weights are transparent, so a reader can argue with the comparison rather than with a coefficient.
when_not_to_use: If the donors cannot reproduce the treated unit before the intervention, the gap afterwards is fit error wearing a policy costume. Weights that pile onto one donor make this a two-unit comparison. With few donors the permutation test cannot produce a small p-value however large the effect, and a donor that had its own shock around the intervention contaminates the comparison. This implementation solves the weight problem with projected gradient plus SLSQP rather than Synth's own solvers, and its cross-validated V is a bounded search, not a global optimum.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

when_to_use: Poor pre-treatment fit is the usual reason a synthetic control fails, and augmentation is the honest response: it estimates the leftover bias and subtracts it, while reporting the uncorrected number beside it so you can see how much of the answer is the correction.
when_not_to_use: The correction can be larger than the original estimate, at which point the outcome model rather than the donor pool is doing the work. The augmented weights can be negative, which means extrapolating outside the donor pool. This implementation offers ridge ASCM only (no covariate or general outcome-model augmentation), picks the penalty by holding out late pre-treatment periods with the SC weights held fixed, and reports placebo inference rather than augsynth's jackknife+ intervals.
The plain synthetic control already fits the pre-treatment period well - then the correction is noise you do not need.

what_it_assumes.title: Pre-treatment fit from the donor pool
what_it_assumes.explains: The weighted combination of untreated units reproduces the treated unit's pre-period path closely enough to stand in for it afterwards.

what_it_assumes.title: No anticipation
what_it_assumes.explains: Units did not change behaviour before treatment arrived because they knew it was coming.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: There was a public announcement well before the policy started, or the pre-period coefficients move in the period immediately before adoption.

what_it_assumes.title: SUTVA / no interference
what_it_assumes.explains: One unit's treatment does not change another unit's outcome, and "treated" means the same thing for everyone who got it.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Units interact: they compete for the same jobs, infect each other, share a classroom or a market. Or the "programme" is really a family of programmes whose intensity varied a lot across sites.

what_it_assumes.title: Parallel trends
what_it_assumes.explains: Without the policy, treated and comparison groups would have moved the same way. Not that they were at the same level -- that their paths would have been parallel.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Pre-period event-study coefficients drift away from zero; the policy was adopted because outcomes were already moving; the groups differ in composition in ways that interact with time.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: It does not need the treated unit to sit inside the donors' convex hull, it uses information from every cell of the panel rather than the treated unit's own history alone, and it handles interactive fixed effects that break parallel trends.
when_not_to_use: There are no donor weights to inspect, so the comparison is much harder to argue with than a synthetic control's. The pre-treatment fit is in-sample and therefore flattering by construction - the placebo-in-time panel is the real check. This implementation uses soft-impute with additive unit and time effects and a single 20% hold-out for the penalty, and its placebo refits reuse that penalty, so the permutation test conditions on it.
Very short panels: with a handful of periods there is no low-rank structure to learn and the fit is mostly the fixed effects.

what_it_assumes.title: Parallel trends
what_it_assumes.explains: Without the policy, treated and comparison groups would have moved the same way. Not that they were at the same level -- that their paths would have been parallel.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: Pre-period event-study coefficients drift away from zero; the policy was adopted because outcomes were already moving; the groups differ in composition in ways that interact with time.

what_it_assumes.title: Consistency / well-defined intervention
what_it_assumes.explains: The outcome you observe under the treatment a unit received is the same as the potential outcome under that treatment. In practice: the treatment has to be a thing someone could actually do.
what_it_assumes.worry_when: The treatment is a state of the world rather than an action, or it is coded from several very different real interventions.

when_to_use: It keeps difference-in-differences' tolerance for a permanent level difference between the treated unit and its comparison while borrowing synthetic control's discipline about which units and which periods count. It is usually less sensitive to a poor level match than classic SC and less sensitive to parallel-trends violations than plain DiD.
when_not_to_use: With one treated unit the paper's jackknife variance is undefined, so inference here is the placebo estimator and rests on donors being exchangeable with the treated unit. Time weights that concentrate on one or two pre-periods make the comparison rest on that slice of history. Covariates are not used at all in this implementation.
Many treated units adopting at different times - use a staggered DiD estimator, which is built for that and gives cohort effects.
